Princess Wolfetka ("Red Apple") seccress of the Cherokee nation, who is an visit to this country to give a series of physic demonstrations, yesterday, (June 23rd) presented the Prince of Wales with a birthday gift, a pair of beaded messesses, made by a "little Indian malden of her tribe. The little guests of the Prince were greatly interested in her stories of the prairies.

OF TOWNSEND ASSUMES HIS FATHER'S TITLE.

Upon the death recently of the Marquis of Townshend, one of the oldest and most popular families of Great Britain, the little five year old son inherits the title of Marquis of Townshend. The late Marquis was one of the most wealthy of England's social set and his little son will now acquire the large fortune. Photo shows the new Marquis in the garden of his London Home. 11/29/21.

Our Readers' Descriptions of the Ideal Husband.
WHAT sort of man does the twentieth century woman admire? The answer is "a true sportsman."

When one comes to think of all that phrase includes, I don't think anyone need look farther. The qualities of the "true sportsman" are:—(1) Chivalry; (2) generosity; (3) capacity for taking hard knocks and for keeping smiling when things are going against him.
Then there is outward appearance. Let me say at once that "good looks" are absolutely unnecessary, but a man must be well-groomed and a particular attention to his hands, a point that
many men neglect. The is one thing a woman cannot forgive a man—effeminacy.
Of course, there a minor points which every one must adjust for their selves, but in general think a true sportsma would please best.
